scenario: A 27-year-old male presents with altered mental status after a suspected intentional amitriptyline overdose, with wide QRS sodium-channel blockade physiology, anticholinergic features, intubation, PEA arrest, and sodium bicarbonate treatment.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I'm getting a heart tracing done right now. Can you tell me what happened today — did you take anything?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I'm getting a heart tracing done right now. Can you tell me what happened today — did you take anything?] fear: not at all->low: The clinician is urgently ordering a heart tracing, signaling something may be wrong with the patient's cardiac status. Even if calmly delivered, the urgency implies a potential cardiac threat, which raises fear from absent to low. shame: not at all->low: The direct question 'did you take anything?' implicitly references possible intentional self-harm or substance use, which is a stigmatized topic that can trigger mild shame even without explicit judgment — especially for a patient with a suspected intentional overdose. sadness and overwhelm: unchanged at not at all — no news of loss or irreversible outcome (sadness), and the utterance is brief with only one clinical action mentioned and one question asked, not enough informational load to trigger overwhelm.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I... I don't really know. My mom found me, I guess. I don't remember much. I'm not sure what happened.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: We're running some blood tests to check his chemistry right now. Can you tell me what you found at the scene — any medications or substances that he might have had access to?

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: ECG result is back: sinus rhythm with a wide QRS complex. Notably, an IV sodium bicarbonate bolus temporarily narrows the QRS.

messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: I didn't find anything — no pills, no bottles, nothing like that in his room. He doesn't take any medications and he has no medical history. I just found him on the floor shaking.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: The ECG shows sinus rhythm with a wide QRS, and that QRS narrowed with the sodium bicarbonate bolus — that's sodium channel blockade until proven otherwise. Give sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg IV bolus right now, then follow with a continuous sodium bicarbonate infusion. We're targeting a serum pH of 7.45 to 7.55 for membrane stabilization.

available_results.name: ECG
available_results.result: Sinus rhythm with wide QRS complex; IV NaHCO3 bolus temporarily changes waveform from wide to narrow QRS complex.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Sodium bicarbonate bolus given. Basic metabolic panel is back: Na 140, K 3.9, Cl 100, bicarb 23, BUN 4.3, creatinine 40, glucose 6.5. I'll get the bicarb infusion running now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: His O2 sat is 90% on room air — place him on a nasal cannula at 4 litres per minute now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: I'm going to place a nasal cannula on you to give you some extra oxygen. You'll feel a light flow of air in your nostrils — it's comfortable and will help your breathing.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: Okay... fine.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Please send a venous blood gas now. We need to monitor pH and keep it in the 7.45 to 7.55 range while the bicarbonate infusion is running.

messages.content: The VBG shows pH 7.29 — that's well below our target of 7.45 to 7.55. Give another sodium bicarbonate bolus, 1 to 2 mEq/kg IV now. Keep the bicarbonate infusion running and recheck the VBG after the bolus.
